service_at_issue: SNF skilled therapy and nursing services after October 5, 2011 (termination of Medicare coverage)
outcome_note: The Council adopted the ALJ decision because the beneficiary did not require skilled services after October 5, 2011 (Jimmo settlement did not change coverage criteria) and she remained liable for non-covered charges after notice.
other_cites: Jimmo v. Sebelius settlement fact sheet
facts: On January 24, 2013, the United States District Court for the District of Vermont approved a settlement agreement in that case, in which the plaintiffs alleged that the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) wrongly applied an “improvement standard” in making skilled care determinations for home health, SNF, and outpatient rehabilitation services. In a Fact Sheet on the litigation, 3 CMS stated that it had denied establishing an improper “rule of thumb” improvement standard and that the Court had not ruled on the plaintiffs’ arguments.

Instead, CMS stated that the Settlement Agreement required that CMS clarify existing policies for consistent and appropriate coverage determinations. See, generally, “Jimmo v. Sebelius Settlement Agreement Fact Sheet,” Attachment.
